newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market rates stable.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market rates stable.

text.p: Dutch money market rates steadied at higher levels on Monday, but dealers said the rates would probably ease later this week because an interest rate rise was not expected.

Dealers said the U.S. dollar's drop from its recent peak and the guilder's strengthening versus the German mark would keep rates unchanged. "We do not see a reason for a rise in official rates, starting in the U.S. or Germany," said one dealer.
U.S. Federal Reserve policy makers are meeting on Tuesday and Germany's Bundesbank will meet on Thursday.
Guilder deposits were unchanged with one-month paper bidding at 3.32 percent and three-month deposits at 3.38 percent.
Call money rates were slightly lower at between 3.25 and 3.31 percent bid versus 3.31 to 3.37 percent last Friday.
Dealers did not expect big movements before Friday's cash reserve expiry.
"Liquidity seems evenly divided among participants," said one dealer, adding he did not foresee any problems in the days to come.
The guilder was a touch stronger versus the German mark at 112.6325 per 100 marks versus 112.635 on Friday.
The U.S. dollar lost further ground, trading at 2.044 guilders versus 2.07 guilders on Friday afternoon.
